# STARBURST audio

**All audio in STARBURST is original and generated by code in this repo.** There are no audio files, samples,
soundfonts or third-party audio libraries, and nothing is fetched from the network: music, stings and sound effects are
synthesised in the browser with the Web Audio API (oscillators, noise, biquad filters, a delay and a small convolution
room built from generated noise). The compositions (chord progressions, bass lines, arps, drum patterns, lead melodies)
were written for this game and live as data in `src/audio/tracks/`.

## Modules

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/audio/dsp.js` | the instruments: kick, snare, clap, hats, toms, tick, bass, arp pluck, lead, pad, riser, crash, bell. Each schedules itself at an audio time and frees its own nodes. Works on a live or an Offline context. |
| `src/audio/rig.js` | per-track mixer: one gain bus per layer (`pad bass kick hat arp snare lead fx`), a tempo-synced echo and a small room as sends. `setLevel(intensity, boss)` opens layers. |
| `src/audio/sequencer.js` | compiles a track definition into bars; `scheduleBar()` turns a bar into voice calls (stateless, shared by live play and offline render); `Sequencer` is the live look-ahead player. |
| `src/audio/tracks/*.js` | the tracks as data (`title.js`, `sectors.js`, `boss.js`), registry in `index.js`, scales in `scales.js`. |
| `src/audio/stings.js` | five one-shot stings as event lists. |
| `src/audio/engine.js` | live music engine (no Phaser): crossfades, intensity, boss mode, ducks, stings, beat queue, analyser. |
| `src/audio/sfx/*.js` | sound-effect recipes (`recipesBase/Combat/Game.js`), per-sample DSP kit, `renderSfx()`. |
| `src/audio/offline.js` | OfflineAudioContext rendering + loudness analysis (used by the tools). |
| `src/systems/music.js` | the game's music API over the engine (`playMusic`, `playSting`, `duck`, `setIntensity`, `setBossMode`, `stopMusic`, `setMusicVolume`). |
| `src/systems/sfx.js` | `sfx(scene, key, opts)`: per-key cooldowns, voice caps, pitch jitter, global voice budget; master glue compressor + limiter. |
| `src/systems/synthSfx.js` | time-sliced bake of every recipe into Phaser's audio cache (+ on-demand render). |
| `src/systems/gameAudio.js` | in-game glue: sector track, intensity, boss theme, stings, low-HP alarm, hum. |
| `src/systems/audioReact.js` | beat / level signals for visuals (beats come from the sequencer, exactly on the audio clock). |
| `tools/render-audio.mjs` | offline render of everything to WAV/MP3 + loudness / loop checks. |
| `audio-lab.html` | dev page to audition everything (served by `npm run dev` at `/audio-lab.html`, not part of the build). |

## How the music works

Tracks are not rendered to buffers: a `Sequencer` schedules synth voices about a second ahead on the audio clock
(`engine.js` pumps it every 120 ms). Consequences: nothing to decode or download, **no loop seam at all** (the pattern
just continues, reverb/echo tails included), and every layer is always in time, so intensity can fade layers in and out.
Main-thread cost is about 1-2.5 ms per bar (measured), 6 ms to start a track.

**Intensity layers** (`setIntensity(0..1)`, see `GATES` in `rig.js`): `pad`, `bass`, `kick` from 0; `arp` from 0.1; `hat`
0.15; `snare` 0.3; `lead` 0.55; `fx` (toms / ticks / crashes) 0.8. Each fades in over the 0.12 below its gate. The bus
low-pass also opens with intensity. **Boss mode** opens everything, opens the filter, adds low end and air.
In a run (`gameAudio.js`) intensity = 20 % global wave progress + 55 % progress through the current sector + 25 % combo,
so every new sector starts calm (pad / bass / kick) and fills out as its waves go by.

**Beats** come from the sequencer (every quarter note, strength 1 on the downbeat, 0.7 on kicks, 0.35 otherwise);
`audioReact.onBeat` / `getPulse` hand them out when their audio time arrives. If the tab was hidden the stale ones are dropped.

### Tracks

All loops are 16 bars. `mood` follows the biome look. Peak/RMS are after the game's master limiter, at full intensity,
before the user's music volume (see Verification).

| Key | Used for | Key / mode | Tempo | Loop | Mood |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title-music` | menus, victory | A minor | 110 BPM | 34.9 s | heroic synthwave: octave bass, rolling arp, theme + bridge |
| `sector1` | Sector 1 NEBULA | F# minor | 118 BPM (light swing) | 32.5 s | dreamy, long echoes, soft pad, sparse lead |
| `sector2` | Sector 2 ASTEROID FIELD | E phrygian | 132 BPM | 29.1 s | heavy, syncopated saw bass, toms, hollow 12.5 % arp |
| `sector3` | Sector 3 DERELICT STATION | C minor | 96 BPM half-time | 40.0 s | cold, sparse, square bass, metal ticks, thin lead |
| `sector4` | Sector 4 SOLAR STORM (and repeats) | G dorian | 150 BPM | 25.6 s | fast, galloping bass, 16th hats, urgent lead |
| `boss` | mid-bosses and bosses | D harmonic minor | 140 BPM | 27.4 s | aggressive riff, double-kick, toms |
| `boss-final` | the final boss | C# phrygian dominant | 150 BPM | 25.6 s | the boss riff pushed: bigger pad, denser kicks |

Sectors past the fourth repeat `sector1..4` like the backdrops do (`sectorTrack()`); the boss theme returns to the sector
track about 2 s after a boss dies.

### Stings

| Key | When | Length |
|---|---|---|
| `sting-boss` | boss warning (with the siren): noise riser into a D-minor slam | 8.5 s |
| `sting-clear` | wave cleared | 3.6 s |
| `sting-gameover` | Game Over screen | 6.2 s |
| `sting-upgrade` | upgrade screen opens | 2.8 s |
| `sting-victory` | victory screen | 9.5 s |

Stings duck the music (`duck('sting')`) while they play.

## Sound effects

Recipes in `src/audio/sfx/` are `{ len, peak, fn }`: `fn(kit)` returns a per-sample function of time. They are rendered once
(deterministic noise) into mono buffers, normalised to `peak` **and** capped at an RMS of -16 dBFS (so one `vol` number
means about the same loudness for every key), and stored in Phaser's audio cache under the key. The bake is time-sliced
(30 ms at boot for menu sounds, the rest in 6 ms idle slices, anything not yet baked is rendered on demand), total about 170 ms.

Weapon voices: `player-shoot` blaster pew, `shoot-spread` fat triple chirp, `shoot-lance` bright zap, `shoot-missile`
whoosh + thump, `shoot-drone` tiny tick, `charge-tick` tier ping, `charge-blast` heavy release. Enemy fire `enemy-shoot`
(lower and duller than the player's). Feedback: `graze` (rate rises with combo), `chain-pop` (pentatonic climb per link of a
chain explosion), `streak` (climbs per 5 kills), `banner`, `pickup` (rate rises with the gem chain), `pickup-repair`,
`pickup-magnet`, `pickup-rapid`, `pickup-x2`, `pickup-shield`, `boss-phase`, `boss-death`, `low-hp` (heartbeat + alarm blip
while hull is under 30 %), `upgrade` / `upgrade-card`, plus the older UI, shield, combo and boss stingers and the
replacements for the old sample set (`dash`, `dash-alt`, `enemy-death(-big)`, `forcefield`, `phase-shift`, `player-damaged`,
`player-death`, `button-sound`, `thruster-hum` (seamless loop), `wave-complete`).

### Mix and anti-fatigue rules

- Signal path: sfx / music buses -> Phaser master volume -> **glue compressor** (-16 dB, 2.5:1: loud sfx pull the music
  down a little, which keeps it "under" them) -> **limiter** (-4 dB, 20:1) -> output. Music sits around -21 dBFS RMS (peaks
  about -8 dB before the limiter), sfx peak at -3 to -9 dBFS; user sliders scale both (master / music / sound in Settings).
- `sfx()` rate-limits per key (`RULES` in `sfx.js`: cooldown, voice cap, default pitch jitter), plays extra voices of the
  same key quieter, and drops the lowest-priority sounds (shots, grazes, hover blips) when 20 voices are already sounding.
- Nothing is started while the tab is hidden or audio is suspended (otherwise the backlog would burst out on return).
  Phaser suspends the context on blur and resumes on focus; `installAudio` also resumes on the first input,
  on `visibilitychange`, and for Safari's `interrupted` state. The sequencer keeps bar alignment across a suspension.

## Auditioning

- `npm run dev`, open `/audio-lab.html`: every track (with intensity / boss / duck controls), sting and sfx (with rate), a live meter.
- In the game (dev build): `__audio.music('sector2')`, `__audio.music('boss', { boss: true })`, `__audio.sting('sting-boss')`,
  `__audio.sfx('graze', { rate: 1.3 })`, `__audio.list()`, `__audio.state()`, `__audio.bake` (boot timing);
  `__dbg.music / sfx / sting` in the Game scene are the same.
- `node tools/render-audio.mjs [--out tmp/audio] [--only sector2,sting-boss,sfx] [--loops 2] [--mp3] [--layers] [--check] [--no-files]`
  renders to WAV (and MP3 with ffmpeg). Music/stings render in headless Chrome (OfflineAudioContext, the same modules the game
  uses); sfx render in Node. A loop file is a true steady-state loop: it includes the previous pass's tails and the wrap
  is sample-exact. `--check` exits 1 on clipping (> -1 dBFS), NaN, silence or a non-periodic loop.
  `tools/make-trailer.mjs` uses it for the trailer soundtrack (`--track boss`).

## Adding a track

1. Create the definition in `src/audio/tracks/` (copy a section of `sectors.js`):
   ```js
   export const myTrack = {
       key: 'my-track', name: 'My Track', bpm: 128, tonic: 'A4', scale: MINOR, swing: 0,
       bassOct: 1, arpOct: 4, padOct: 3, gain: 0.8,           // gain trims the whole track
       mix: { pad: 0.5, bass: 0.9, kick: 0.9, snare: 0.7, hat: 0.4, arp: 0.5, lead: 0.5, fx: 0.5 },
       sections: [{ bars: 4, prog: 'Am F C G', bass: 'x.o.x.o.x.o.x.o.', arp: '0123432101234321',
                    lead: '8:4 7:2 5:2 3:4 5:4  6:4 8:2 6:2 5:4 3:4  ...',   // 'degree:steps', 16 steps per bar
                    drums: { k: 'x...x...x...x...', s: '....x.......x...', h: 'x.x.x.x.x.x.x.x.' } }]
   };
   ```
   Patterns are 16-step strings per bar (an array cycles per bar). Bass: `x` root, `o` octave, `f` fifth, `s` flat seventh.
   Arp digits index the chord stack. Drums: `x` hit, `g` ghost, hat row `o` open hat, fx row `t` tick `m`/`M` toms `c` clap.
   Chords: `Am`, `F`, `C#5`, `Bb`, `F#m7`, `Csus`, `Bdim`. Section flags: `crash`, `fill`, `padHalf`, `pad: false`, `leadVoice`.
2. Register it in `src/audio/tracks/index.js` (that also makes it appear in the lab page and the render tool).
3. `node tools/render-audio.mjs --check --layers --only my-track`: fix anything flagged, trim `gain` until the RMS is about -21 dBFS.
4. Play it: `playMusic('my-track')`, or add it to `sectorTrack()` / `GameAudio` if it should play automatically.

To add a sting, add an entry to `STINGS` in `stings.js`; for an sfx, add a recipe to one of `recipes*.js` (the key is the
cache key; give it a rule in `sfx.js` if it can fire often).

## Verification (no ears needed)

`node tools/render-audio.mjs --check --layers` renders every track (3 passes, the first is a warm-up) and reports peak, RMS,
NaN count, DC, pass-to-pass difference and the seam; the numbers below are from the final run.

RESULTS_PLACEHOLDER

What a human still has to judge by ear: melodic taste, whether each sector track feels like its backdrop, the balance of the
layers (the lab page's intensity slider), the mix of music vs. sfx in a real fight, and the pitch climb of the chain / streak sounds.
